summary: Integration tests for all three observability pipelines (metrics, logfwd, auditfwd) validating MultiReporter dual delivery, error isolation, credential resolution, and TLS skip-verify behavior. 21 integration tests total (9 metrics, 6 logfwd, 6 auditfwd) using httptest.NewTLSServer for realistic TLS behavior. No production code modified. Reference documentation added for test patterns and coverage matrix.

tests_checklist.item: V1: All tests pass (`go test -race` — 0 failures, 0 data races)
TE1: Happy path tested with realistic dual delivery via full Manager/Forwarder.Run loop
TE2: Edge cases covered — empty URL (platform-only), self-signed TLS strict/skip-verify, credential failure
TE3: Error cases tested — HTTP 500, credential resolution failure, TLS handshake failure
TE4: Tests independent — no shared mutable state, each test creates fresh servers and reporters
TE5: Test names follow project convention (TestIntegration_Subject_Behavior)
TE6: Mocking appropriate — httptest.NewTLSServer for local, in-memory mock for platform
TE7: Assertions specific — exact HTTP method, Content-Type, Authorization header, JSON deserialization, batch element counts

code_quality_checklist.item: Q1: Helper functions do one thing (httpCapture.handler, httpCapture.count, waitFor)
Q2: Functions small — all under 40 lines

Q3: HTTP capture pattern duplicated across 3 packages (httpCapture, logHTTPCapture, auditHTTPCapture) — acceptable because these are white-box tests in separate packages that cannot share unexported types
Q4: Clear naming — test names describe scenario and expectation
Q5: No deep nesting — guard clauses with t.Fatal/t.Skip used
Q7: No dead code or commented-out code
P1: Follows existing test patterns (testNSK, encryptTestSecret, discardLogger reused)
P2: Uses existing utilities from local_reporter_test.go
P5: File location follows convention (integration_test.go in each pipeline package)

security_checklist.item: S3: No hardcoded secrets — test tokens are obviously fake ('integration-token', 'tok', 'tls-tok')
S5: No sensitive data exposure in test output

architecture_checklist.item: Solution is as simple as possible — white-box tests reusing existing helpers
Tests exercise the real wiring pattern from up.go (conditional MultiReporter construction)

dry_yagni_checklist.item: HTTP capture helpers necessarily duplicated across packages (separate Go packages cannot share unexported test types)
No over-engineering — test infrastructure is minimal (capture struct, waitFor poll)
Metrics has 2 extra tests (platform-only, conditional wiring) not duplicated in logfwd/auditfwd since the pattern is identical

fail_fast_checklist.item: Tests use t.Fatal for setup failures, t.Error for assertion failures
waitFor helper has 3-second timeout with clear failure message
testing.Short() skip prevents slow tests in quick CI loops

defensive_checklist.item: All httpCapture access is mutex-protected (thread-safe for concurrent test goroutines)
Context cancellation and goroutine draining properly handled in all Run-loop tests

suggested_improvements: Q3-minor: The httpCapture/capturedRequest types are structurally identical across all 3 packages (only prefixed differently). If a future shared internal/testutil package is introduced, these could be consolidated. Not actionable now since Go test packages cannot import each other's unexported types.
TE-minor: The waitFor helper uses a busy-loop with time.Sleep(5ms). A ticker-based approach would be marginally cleaner but functionally equivalent for test code.
D2-minor: The metrics integration_test.go has 486 lines vs 351 for logfwd/auditfwd — the extra 135 lines cover the platform-only and conditional wiring tests that are correctly unique to metrics.
